summary:
Chandīgarh is a union territory of India and stands under the national framework as it applies to the territory. The source inventory for this record contains no Chandīgarh-specific laws, incidents, institutions or documented practice concerning transgender visitors; the assessment therefore rests on the national layer carried by the parent record.

Under the national framework, India's Parliament passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill on 25 March 2026, with presidential assent pending at the time of the source's reporting. If assented, the amendment removes the self-identification right affirmed by the Supreme Court's 2014 judgment, limits legal recognition to historically accepted socio-cultural categories and intersex people, narrows recognition to male and female categories plus traditional identities, and makes medical-board and district-authority certification mandatory for gender-affirming surgery. It adds offences carrying up to life imprisonment for 'coercing or alluring' people to be transgender, amending the 2019 law. Critics warn the narrower definition excludes self-identifying gender-fluid and non-binary people; the People's Union for Civil Liberties warns the new offences echo colonial-era criminalisation of transgender people. The bill was passed amid protests in Mumbai, and about two million transgender people live in India.
tangentialFactors:
The territory's own record holds no incidents of police conduct, checkpoint friction or documented violence against transgender people; assessments of such conduct in the national inventory derive from other states and cities and are carried by the parent record.

No Chandīgarh-specific welfare board, healthcare scheme administration, or facility-access rule appears in the inventory. Whether the union territory runs its own transgender welfare measures, or administers national schemes such as Ayushman Bharat locally, is not sourced here.
localsOnly:
Residents of Chandīgarh stand under the same national recognition and certification regime described for visitors, since the amendment's scope is national. The inventory records no Chandīgarh-specific procedure, office or authority handling gender-marker changes, medical certification or district-authority documentation for residents.

No Chandīgarh-specific policing guideline, sensitisation programme, conversion-therapy ban or judicial order appears in the inventory. Whether the territory has adopted measures comparable to those issued by other state high courts or state welfare boards is not sourced here.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether presidential assent to the March 2026 amendment has been given, and the territory-level implementation status of the amended recognition scheme in Chandīgarh, are unresolved in this inventory.

Chandīgarh-specific enforcement practice, detention treatment, facility access and welfare administration are not sourced; the record carries no territory-level signal beyond the national framework.
